summary: NXDOMAIN negative cache on corporate DNS forwarder causing control-plane artifact pull backoff in private deploy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent control-plane timeouts and repeated model artifact pull backoffs from serving nodes. Impact: Customer's private deployment (VPC-connected) observed model download failures and extended GC backoff; model-serving pods enter Trailing state for up to 2-5 minutes causing request 5xxs and increased latency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private agent connected via AWS Transit Gateway to customer VPC
2) Trigger a model rollout that requires artifact pulls (large model) across the agent nodes
3) Observe agent logs where initial DNS resolution for s3-presigned host returns NXDOMAIN intermittently
4) Serving runtime retries; control-plane backoff increases and artifact pulls are delayed or aborted
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T14:01:13Z agent[model-fetch] WARN: artifact fetch attempt 3 failed; backoff=13s
2026-03-10T14:03:25Z serving-runtime ERROR: model load failed due to artifact fetch timeout
Control-plane trace: request_id=abc123; control-plane retried DNS A lookup 7 times before failing
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed failures correlate with NXDOMAIN answers in VPC egress path; customer uses an on-prem forwarder over an IPSEC tunnel for corporate DNS resolution.
Packet capture from customer side shows responses with RCODE=3 (NXDOMAIN) and long TTL in SOA negative caching (SOA MINIMUM/negative-ttl=3600s).

Hypothesis: Corporate forwarder is returning NXDOMAIN for our presigned host intermittently (due to internal split-horizon rules) and client machines are obeying negative TTL, causing prolonged negative cache hits and repeated artifact fetch backoffs.
Verified agent DNS resolver order: /etc/resolv.conf -> 10.0.2.5 (customer-forwarder) -> AmazonProvidedDNS; Negative response observed only from 10.0.2.5.
Correlated spike windows with customer's internal DNS failover events (their DNS server rotation during maintenance appears to return NXDOMAIN briefly).
customer_impact_summary: Multiple model pulls failed across several serving nodes in customer VPC between 14:00-14:15 UTC; customers reported 5xxs for production traffic and inability to load a new model_version. Estimated user-facing downtime window: ~12 minutes for affected nodes.
temporary_workaround: 1) Instructed customer to flush negative cache entries on their forwarder (bind/named: rndc flushname s3-presigned.example.com and reduce negative-caching TTL),
2) Applied control-plane configuration to prefer EDNS-aware recursive resolver (moved resolv.conf to explicit AmazonProvidedDNS in agent for the fetch process only) as a short-term mitigation
3) Restarted artifact fetch service on affected nodes to clear internal resolver caches
long_term_recommendations: 1) Customer should disable long negative-caching for split-horizon zones containing Redwood artifact hosts or ensure authoritative responses are correct across their forwarders
2) Add DNS resiliency in agent: consult multiple upstreams and treat NXDOMAIN from a single forwarder as soft-failure for 30s before caching globally
3) Documented a runbook for agents in private deploys to override egress resolver for artifact fetches or use fallback public DNS when presigned urls are involved
4) Consider telemetry addition: alert when NXDOMAIN negative cache TTL > 300s on artifact domains
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC: Customer IT team patched their forwarder to return NOERROR with CNAME to correct presigned host during rotate (temporary fix),
2026-03-11 11:30 UTC: Support applied a staged agent config change to prefer AmazonProvidedDNS for artifact pulls (hotfix).
Outcome: Artifact pulls resumed and backoff counters cleared; serving nodes recovered and model loads completed within 10 minutes of mitigation.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to create a code change to make agent DNS resolver order configurable per-subsystem (PR referenced below),
2) Support to follow up with customer in 72 hours to confirm no recurrence,
3) Product to evaluate default agent behavior for DNS in private deployments and add documentation guidance
4) Security review: ensure allowing public DNS for artifact fetches does not violate customer policy (customer approved temporary change)
